# Cisco AI Defense Intercept Plugin The **AI Defense Intercept** plugin (`ai-defense-intercept`) intercepts AI/LLM and [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) traffic on Kong Gateway and submits prompts, completions, and tool calls to **Cisco AI Defense** for inspection before allowing them through. It blocks or forwards traffic based on the AI Defense verdict. It operates in two phases: - **Access phase** — inspects the client request (prompt / MCP tool call) before forwarding upstream. - **Response phase** — inspects the upstream response (completion / MCP tool result) before returning it to the client. ## How it works The plugin captures the request and/or response, transforms it into the inspection payload expected by AI Defense (per the configured profile), calls the AI Defense inspection API, and enforces the verdict (`Allow` → forward, `Block` → block). The plugin priority is **1000** (it runs early, after authentication plugins such as `key-auth`). ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant Client participant Kong as Kong Gateway
ai-defense-intercept participant AID as Cisco AI Defense
Inspection API participant Upstream as Upstream (LLM / MCP server) Client->>Kong: Request (prompt / MCP tools/call) Kong->>Kong: Build inspection payload (per profile) Kong->>AID: Inspect request AID-->>Kong: Verdict (Allow / Block) alt Block Kong->>Client: Block response (standard error envelope) else Allow Kong->>Upstream: Forward request Upstream-->>Kong: Response (completion / tool result) Kong->>Kong: Buffer + build inspection payload Kong->>AID: Inspect response AID-->>Kong: Verdict (Allow / Block) alt Block Kong->>Client: Block response (standard error envelope) else Allow Kong->>Client: Upstream response end end ``` ### Profiles The `profile` selects sensible payload defaults for the kind of traffic on the route. An explicit `request_payload_mode` / `response_payload_mode` always overrides the profile default. | Profile | Use case | Request payload | Response payload | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `model` | OpenAI-compatible chat / Bedrock Converse | `chat_messages` | `chat_messages` | | `mcp` | Model Context Protocol (JSON-RPC) | `raw_body` | `mcp_jsonrpc` | | `custom` (default) | Anything else | `raw_body` | `inspection_envelope` | Payload modes: - **`chat_messages`** — extracts `{ "messages": [{ "role", "content" }] }` from OpenAI chat completions and Bedrock Converse (request and response shapes), normalizing multipart content. - **`mcp_jsonrpc`** — sends the MCP JSON-RPC message. For **responses**, the plugin merges the originating request's `method` and `params` with the response `result`/`error` (`{ jsonrpc, id, method, params, result }`), because the AI Defense MCP inspector requires `method`/`params` for response inspection. Handles direct JSON-RPC and SSE-wrapped payloads. - **`raw_body`** — sends the raw request/response body unchanged. - **`inspection_envelope`** — wraps the body in a `tools/call` JSON-RPC envelope with configurable inspection name / payload field. ### MCP control-message bypass MCP JSON-RPC handshake/control messages (`initialize`, `initialized`, `ping`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list`) carry no scannable content, so the plugin **bypasses** inspection for them (and their responses) by default. Configure via `mcp_bypass_control_methods` and `mcp_control_methods`. ### Verdict The decision is driven by the AI Defense `action` field (`Allow` → allowed, `Block` → blocked), read from the top level or nested under `result`. A non-2xx response, transport failure, or unparseable body is treated as an **operational error** (not a content verdict) and routed through the fail-open / fail-closed path. ### Resilience - **Fail mode** — `fail_closed` (default `true`) blocks traffic when inspection is unavailable; set `false` to fail open (forward uninspected, with skip headers). - **Retries** — `max_retries` retries transport-level callout failures (not HTTP status codes). - **Circuit breaker** — after `circuit_breaker_failures` consecutive failures the plugin stops calling AI Defense for `circuit_breaker_cooldown_seconds` and applies the fail mode directly. - **Metrics** — when `metrics` is enabled, `kong_ai_defense_*` counters/histograms are published on Kong's bundled Prometheus exporter (`/metrics`). ## Configuration reference | Parameter | Required | Default | Description | | --- | :--: | --- | --- | | `profile` | No | `custom` | `custom` \| `mcp` \| `model` — selects payload defaults. | | `defense_url` | **Yes** | — | AI Defense inspection endpoint. Must be `https://`. | | `defense_api_key` | No¹ | — | AI Defense API key. Encrypted + referenceable (use a Vault reference). | | `defense_api_key_source_header` | No¹ | — | Header to read the AI Defense key from per request (stripped before upstream). | | `defense_api_key_header` | No | `X-Cisco-AI-Defense-API-Key` | Header used to send the key to AI Defense. | | `defense_headers` | No | `{}` | Extra headers sent to AI Defense. | | `timeout` | No | `10000` | Callout timeout (ms), 100–60000. | | `fail_closed` | No | `true` | Block traffic when inspection is unavailable. | | `block_status` | No | `400` | HTTP status for blocked/errored traffic, 400–599. | | `check_request` | No | `true` | Inspect the request. | | `check_response` | No | `true` | Inspect the response. | | `request_payload_mode` | No | (profile) | `raw_body` \| `inspection_envelope` \| `chat_messages`. | | `response_payload_mode` | No | (profile) | `raw_body` \| `inspection_envelope` \| `chat_messages` \| `mcp_jsonrpc`. | | `ssl_verify` | No | `true` | Verify the AI Defense TLS certificate. | | `max_body_bytes` | No | `10485760` (10 MiB) | Maximum request/response bytes inspected. For requests, bounds file-backed body reads; `0` disables the plugin limit. | | `max_retries` | No | `1` | Extra retries on transport callout failure, 0–5. | | `keepalive_pool` | No | `10` | Keepalive connection pool size to AI Defense. | | `circuit_breaker` | No | `true` | Enable the circuit breaker. | | `circuit_breaker_failures` | No | `5` | Consecutive failures before opening, 1–1000. | | `circuit_breaker_cooldown_seconds` | No | `30` | Open duration, 1–3600. | | `metrics` | No | `true` | Publish `kong_ai_defense_*` via the bundled Prometheus plugin. | | `shared_dict` | No | `ai_defense` | `lua_shared_dict` for cross-worker breaker/metrics state. | | `mcp_bypass_control_methods` | No | `true` | Skip inspection for MCP control messages. | | `mcp_control_methods` | No | (handshake list) | MCP methods treated as control messages. | | `propagate_request_id` | No | `true` | Send the Kong request id to AI Defense and reflect it to the client. | | `request_inspection_name` / `response_inspection_name` | No | `kong_request_inspection` / `kong_response_inspection` | Envelope inspection names (`inspection_envelope` mode). | | `request_payload_field` / `response_payload_field` | No | `request` / `response` | Envelope payload field names (`inspection_envelope` mode). | ¹ At least one of `defense_api_key` or `defense_api_key_source_header` is required. ## Block / error response format All plugin-generated responses use a consistent, versioned envelope. Detail stays in logs and response headers; the body is intentionally generic so it never leaks inspection internals or detected content to the caller. ```json { "error": { "code": "AI_DEFENSE_RESPONSE_BLOCKED", "message": "Response blocked by Cisco AI Defense Policy.", "decision": "block", "phase": "response", "transaction_id": "a1b2c3d4-..." } } ``` | `code` | `decision` | When | | --- | --- | --- | | `AI_DEFENSE_REQUEST_BLOCKED` / `AI_DEFENSE_RESPONSE_BLOCKED` | `block` | AI Defense returned `Block`. | | `AI_DEFENSE_REQUEST_UNAVAILABLE` / `AI_DEFENSE_RESPONSE_UNAVAILABLE` | `error` | Fail-closed: inspection unavailable / errored. | | `AI_DEFENSE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | `error` | Body exceeds `max_body_bytes`. | Response headers on every plugin-generated response: | Header | Description | | --- | --- | | `x-ai-defense-decision` | `block` or `error` | | `x-ai-defense-phase` | `request` or `response` | | `x-ai-defense-categories` | Comma-separated triggering rulesets (e.g. `PII,Prompt Injection`), when available | | `x-ai-defense-transaction-id` | Correlation id; matches the AI Defense / orchestrator logs | AI Defense policy blocks and fail-closed response inspection errors use the configurable `block_status` (default `400`). Request payload-size errors use `413`; other fail-closed request inspection errors use `502`. Use `decision` / `code` — not status alone — to distinguish a policy block from an inspection failure. ## Install The plugin can be deployed three ways. For **production**, prefer the **custom Docker image** (this repository's model — the plugin, and optionally the declarative config, are baked in and immutable). Use the **volume mount** for local development. ### Prerequisites - Kong Gateway 3.4 or later (this repo builds on `kong/kong-gateway:3.14`). - Kong 3.9.2 and later can read file-backed request bodies through the PDK; older supported versions use a bounded read of Nginx's cached body file. - A Cisco AI Defense inspection endpoint (`https://`) and API key. - Network egress from Kong to the AI Defense endpoint. - If you configure an Nginx `client_max_body_size` cap, keep it at least as high as the plugin's `max_body_bytes` limit. - An `lua_shared_dict` named `ai_defense` for cross-worker circuit-breaker / metrics state (`KONG_NGINX_HTTP_LUA_SHARED_DICT="ai_defense 16m"`). Copy the plugin files (`handler.lua`, `schema.lua`) from `plugins/ai-defense-intercept/`. ### Kong Konnect: upload the plugin schema For Konnect-managed control planes, upload the plugin schema once via the Control Planes API, then deploy the plugin files to your data plane using one of the options below. ```sh export KONNECT_TOKEN="[REDACTED]" export CONTROL_PLANE_ID="your-control-plane-id" curl -X POST \ "https://us.api.konghq.com/v2/control-planes/${CONTROL_PLANE_ID}/core-entities/plugin-schemas" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KONNECT_TOKEN}" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"lua_schema\": $(jq -Rs '.' schema.lua)}" ``` ### Option 1 — Docker with volume mount (development) Mount the plugin source into a stock Kong Gateway image and enable it. Recommended for **development only** (the plugin is mounted at runtime, not baked in). ```yaml # docker-compose.yml services: kong: image: kong/kong-gateway:3.14 environment: KONG_PLUGINS: "bundled,ai-defense-intercept" KONG_NGINX_HTTP_LUA_SHARED_DICT: "ai_defense 16m" volumes: - ./plugins/ai-defense-intercept:/usr/local/share/lua/5.1/kong/plugins/ai-defense-intercept:ro ``` ```bash docker compose up -d ``` ### Option 2 — Custom Docker image (production, recommended) Bake the plugin into the image so it is self-contained and reproducible: ```dockerfile FROM kong/kong-gateway:3.14 USER root COPY plugins/ai-defense-intercept /usr/local/share/lua/5.1/kong/plugins/ai-defense-intercept RUN chown -R kong:kong /usr/local/share/lua/5.1/kong/plugins/ai-defense-intercept USER kong ENV KONG_PLUGINS=bundled,ai-defense-intercept ENV KONG_NGINX_HTTP_LUA_SHARED_DICT="ai_defense 16m" ENV KONG_NGINX_HTTP_CLIENT_MAX_BODY_SIZE=100m ``` ```bash docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t /ai-defense-kong-plugin: . docker push /ai-defense-kong-plugin: ``` This repository's [`docker/Dockerfile`](../docker/Dockerfile) additionally bakes the declarative config as a template and renders secrets at startup — see the [README](../README.md). ### Option 3 — Kubernetes **Recommended:** deploy the custom image from Option 2 (plugin baked in): ```yaml containers: - name: kong-gateway image: /ai-defense-kong-plugin: env: - name: KONG_PLUGINS value: "bundled,ai-defense-intercept" - name: KONG_NGINX_HTTP_LUA_SHARED_DICT value: "ai_defense 16m" ``` **Alternative — mount the plugin via a ConfigMap** (use a stock Kong image without rebuilding): ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: ai-defense-intercept-plugin data: handler.lua: | # paste plugins/ai-defense-intercept/handler.lua contents here schema.lua: | # paste plugins/ai-defense-intercept/schema.lua contents here --- apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: kong spec: template: spec: containers: - name: kong image: kong/kong-gateway:3.14 env: - name: KONG_PLUGINS value: "bundled,ai-defense-intercept" - name: KONG_NGINX_HTTP_LUA_SHARED_DICT value: "ai_defense 16m" volumeMounts: - name: plugin mountPath: /usr/local/share/lua/5.1/kong/plugins/ai-defense-intercept volumes: - name: plugin configMap: name: ai-defense-intercept-plugin ``` ### Verify the plugin is loaded ```bash # Plugin files present docker exec ls -la /usr/local/share/lua/5.1/kong/plugins/ai-defense-intercept/ # Plugin enabled docker exec printenv KONG_PLUGINS # Plugin referenced in logs / Admin API docker logs 2>&1 | grep -i "ai-defense-intercept" curl -s http://localhost:8001/ | grep -o ai-defense-intercept # Admin API (keep private) ``` You should see both `handler.lua` and `schema.lua`. ## Enable Cisco AI Defense Intercept Once installed, enable the plugin on a service or route. The only required setting is `defense_url`; supply the AI Defense API key via `defense_api_key` (a Vault reference) or `defense_api_key_source_header`. Pick the method that matches how you run Kong. ### Declarative (DB-less) ```yaml plugins: - name: ai-defense-intercept config: profile: model defense_url: https:///api/v1/inspect/chat defense_api_key_source_header: X-Cisco-AI-Defense-API-Key fail_closed: true check_request: true check_response: true ``` ### Admin API (DB-backed Kong Gateway) ```sh curl -X POST http://localhost:8001/services//plugins \ --data "name=ai-defense-intercept" \ --data "config.profile=model" \ --data "config.defense_url=https:///api/v1/inspect/chat" \ --data "config.defense_api_key_source_header=X-Cisco-AI-Defense-API-Key" ``` ### Kong Konnect ```sh curl -X POST \ "https://us.api.konghq.com/v2/control-planes/${CONTROL_PLANE_ID}/core-entities/plugins" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KONNECT_TOKEN}" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "name": "ai-defense-intercept", "service": {"id": "YOUR_SERVICE_ID"}, "config": { "profile": "model", "defense_url": "https:///api/v1/inspect/chat", "defense_api_key_source_header": "X-Cisco-AI-Defense-API-Key" } }' ``` For the AI Defense key, prefer a Kong [Vault reference](https://docs.konghq.com/gateway/latest/kong-enterprise/secrets-management/) (`defense_api_key: "[REDACTED]}"`) or supply it per request via `defense_api_key_source_header`. Never hardcode the key. ## Test Allowed request (chat route): ```bash curl -i http://localhost:8000/model/inspection \ -H 'apikey: [REDACTED]' \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -H 'X-Cisco-AI-Defense-API-Key: [REDACTED]' \ -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 2+2?"}]}' ``` A request whose prompt violates policy returns the block envelope with HTTP `block_status`: ```json { "error": { "code": "AI_DEFENSE_REQUEST_BLOCKED", "message": "Request blocked by Cisco AI Defense Policy.", "decision": "block", "phase": "request", "transaction_id": "..." } } ``` ## Observe Logs (the plugin logs verdicts, categories, and the AI Defense response body on non-2xx): ```bash # Docker docker logs 2>&1 | grep -i "ai-defense-intercept" # Kubernetes kubectl logs -f deploy/ai-defense-kong-plugin | grep -i "ai-defense-intercept" ``` Correlate a client-visible `transaction_id` with the AI Defense / orchestrator logs to see the full verdict (rulesets, scores). Metrics: when `metrics` is enabled and the bundled `prometheus` plugin is on, `kong_ai_defense_*` series appear on Kong's `/metrics` endpoint (decisions, errors, fail-mode, circuit-breaker events, retries, callout latency). ## Limitations - Response inspection requires response buffering (enabled automatically when `check_response` is true). - Inspection callouts are synchronous, bounded by `timeout` (default 10s). - `block_status` applies to both blocks and fail-closed errors; callers differentiate via `decision` / `code`. - The response phase cannot change the HTTP status once response headers have been sent by the upstream in non-buffered paths. ## Security considerations - Store the AI Defense key in a Vault reference or inject it per request; never bake it into the image or config. - Keep `ssl_verify: true` in production. - Keep the Kong Admin API private (loopback / internal only); expose only the proxy port. - Review blocked traffic and circuit-breaker events; alert on elevated `ai_defense_errors_total` / `ai_defense_fail_mode_total`. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Check | | --- | --- | | Plugin not loading | `docker exec ls /usr/local/share/lua/5.1/kong/plugins/ai-defense-intercept/`; confirm `KONG_PLUGINS` includes `ai-defense-intercept`. | | Everything returns the block envelope | Inspection is failing and `fail_closed=true`. Check logs for the AI Defense response body (now logged on non-2xx) and verify `defense_url` / key. | | PII/violations not blocked | Confirm the content reaches the inspected payload (esp. MCP, where only the prompt string is scanned), and that the AI Defense **policy** for your tenant enforces (blocks) the ruleset rather than monitors it. | | MCP response inspection 400 (`requires method and params`) | Ensure `response_payload_mode: mcp_jsonrpc` (the plugin merges request `method`/`params` into the response payload). | | Reason shows only `Block` | Upgrade to the standardized error format; the triggering rulesets appear in `x-ai-defense-categories` / logs. | ## Related resources - [Repository README](../README.md) — build the custom image, run locally, deploy. - [Cisco AI Defense](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/products/security/ai-defense/index.html)

# Security Policies and Procedures

This document outlines security procedures and general policies for the
`ai-defense-kong-plugin` project.

- [Disclosing a security issue](#disclosing-a-security-issue)
- [Vulnerability management](#vulnerability-management)
- [Suggesting changes](#suggesting-changes)

## Disclosing a security issue

The `ai-defense-kong-plugin` maintainers take all security issues in the project
seriously. Thank you for improving the security of `ai-defense-kong-plugin`. We
appreciate your dedication to responsible disclosure and will make every effort
to acknowledge your contributions.

`ai-defense-kong-plugin` leverages GitHub's private vulnerability reporting.

To learn more about this feature and how to submit a vulnerability report,
review [GitHub's documentation on private reporting](https://docs.github.com/code-security/security-advisories/guidance-on-reporting-and-writing-information-about-vulnerabilities/privately-reporting-a-security-vulnerability).

Here are some helpful details to include in your report:

- a detailed description of the issue
- the steps required to reproduce the issue
- versions of the project that may be affected by the issue
- if known, any mitigations for the issue

A maintainer will acknowledge the report within three (3) business days, and
will send a more detailed response within an additional three (3) business days
indicating the next steps in handling your report.

If you've been unable to successfully draft a vulnerability report via GitHub
or have not received a response during the allotted response window, please
reach out via the [Cisco Open security contact email](mailto:oss-security@cisco.com).

After the initial reply to your report, the maintainers will endeavor to keep
you informed of the progress towards a fix and full announcement, and may ask
for additional information or guidance.

## Vulnerability management

When the maintainers receive a disclosure report, they will assign it to a
primary handler.

This person will coordinate the fix and release process, which involves the
following steps:

- confirming the issue
- determining affected versions of the project
- auditing code to find any potential similar problems
- preparing fixes for all releases under maintenance

## Suggesting changes

If you have suggestions on how this process could be improved please submit an
issue or pull request.

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v5.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: trailing-whitespace
  - repo: https://github.com/google/addlicense
    rev: 4529cd558fa0bf07ab0f2650e36d089fb1c07c89
    hooks:
      - id: addlicense
        args: [ "-v", "-s",
                "-c", "Cisco Systems, Inc. and its affiliates",
                "-l", "apache",
                "plugins" ]
        types: [ lua ]
